# Best portable power station for a CPAP

**My pick for most people: BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh).** [Buy the BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) for $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF (price tested Oct 21, per [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-portable-power-station-for-cpap-machine-2026-runtime-humidifier-pure-sine-w)).

- **Runtime:** About 3 nights with no humidifier and about 1.4 nights with a heated humidifier, assuming roughly 40 W dry and 90 W humidified ([BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/), [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap)).
- **Drawbacks:** It weighs about 16 kg, and Dealectric's record doesn't state the waveform. Confirm pure sine with BLUETTI before buying. Most 2026 stations are pure sine, but check ([PowerStationTips](https://powerstationtips.com/articles/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).

## Other options

| Need | Pick | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Small, one-night backup, no humidifier | [Tenergy T320](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-t320-300wh-power-station), $225.99 | 300 Wh, explicitly pure sine, 200 W, LiFePO4. Wall recharge takes about 8 hours. |
| Small with fast recharge | [BLUETTI Elite 30 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2), $275.50 with code AFF5OFF | 288 Wh, full recharge in about 70 minutes. Waveform not stated, so confirm it. |
| Quietest, best for the bedside | Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, about $700 | About 20 dB under 200 W, 10 ms UPS switchover, about 1.7 humidified nights ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)). |
| CPAP plus home backup | EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus, about $719 | Expandable capacity ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)). |
| Travel at about 1 kWh | Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, about $499 | Lightest 1 kWh pick ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)). |

I don't have verified direct buy links for the Anker, EcoFlow, and Jackery units. The review pages above list store links for them.

## Key points

- **Size for runtime:** Divide the station's Wh by your machine's watts (check its label). Real-world runtime will be lower. A 300 Wh unit like the Tenergy T320 covers only about 0.8 of a night, so it's a stopgap, not a multi-night solution.
- **Humidifier:** A heated humidifier roughly doubles the draw. If you use one, halve the runtime figures, or use the machine's DC cable or turn the heater off during outages.
- **UPS switchover:** If you want therapy to continue when the grid drops mid-sleep, look for about 10 ms or faster.
- The Dealectric links are affiliate links. Most of the reviews I drew on are research-based, not hands-on lab tests.
- This is general information, not medical advice. If you depend on CPAP, ask your equipment supplier about backup power.

Tell me your CPAP model and whether you use the heated humidifier, and I can narrow this to one pick.
